why: the rule's only MET branch: tail clears, correlation negative, tail positive in both evaluable years. Bear R is exactly minus deployed R on every date, so the correlation is -1 by construction and needs no estimate. Worst decile = max(3, 24//10) = 3 dates, which sort to dep -0.30 (2024), -0.30 (2025), -0.20 (2024), so bear on the tail is +0.30, +0.30, +0.20 = 0.8/3

the mirror of d2_met with bear R set equal to deployed R rather than its negative: the sleeve loses on exactly the days the book does. Correlation +1, tail bear R = (-0.30 -0.30 -0.20)/3, no year's worst quartile positive. Two clauses fail at once, which is the point — the rule is an AND

the year clause carrying the whole verdict: the pooled tail is +2.0 and the correlation is negative, so the rule turns on 2025 alone. Deployed R is -1 on six dates a year and +1 on six; bear is +2 on every 2024 losing date and on 2025's last three but -2 on 2025's first three. Correlation by hand: sum(xy) = -24, sxx = 24, syy = 60, so r = -24/sqrt(1440) = -1/sqrt(2.5)

d2_met plus five 2026 dates above every other date. A year under six overlapping dates is REPORTED and not COUNTED: 2026 enters neither ok_years nor tot_years, so the verdict is still 2/2 and MET. The five dates do not change the tail either — max(3, 29//10) is still 3

no deployed date is negative, so the negative-dates cut is EMPTY and the bucket list is four rows rather than five — an empty cut is dropped, never printed as a zero. Exactly 20 overlapping dates, so it also pins the power floor's boundary: 20 is evaluated. The tail is the three lowest, bear -0.0 -0.1 -0.2

six overlapping dates against the default floor of 20: the cell is not evaluated at all and the criterion returns nothing. A study prints its own skip line — the library refuses to hand back figures nobody may quote

d2_empty_bucket_is_dropped with the lowest date's bear value undefined, as a caller carrying an unfillable date hands it over. Every comparison against nan is False, so the tail clause and the correlation clause both fail and the verdict is NOT MET — the rule fails CLOSED rather than passing vacuously, which is the bug that sat in bear_deploy's D1 window check until 2026-08-24

the sweep's whole point: f=1.00 turns the book's best day into its worst (-250 against a -200 baseline) and fails both comparisons, while 0.25 and 0.50 clear them, so the criterion takes 0.50 and not the largest tested size. The sleeve also carries a date the book is flat on (01-06), which costs dollars at every f — the union of dates, not the book's. Least-harmful ties at -125 between 0.25 and 0.50 and goes to the first

an always-on sleeve that bleeds on every date: each fraction deepens the drawdown past the baseline, so no size clears the rule and the criterion returns none rather than the closest one. The least-harmful size is reported separately as context and is the smallest tested fraction here

an empty sleeve leaves every fraction identical to the baseline, so the rule passes at the LARGEST fraction while nothing is hedged. Recorded so that fail-open is visible and cannot change unnoticed — a study reads the position count beside the verdict for exactly this reason. Also pins the downside deviation as the RMS of the negative days only: sqrt((900+1600)/2), and the drawdown of a curve that never gets above flat

one position a day by the picker's key. 01-02 takes the higher key; 01-03's unrankable row is dropped but the day still fills from the other; 01-04's highest-key row has no dollars so it was never a candidate; 01-05 has no rankable row at all and the day is skipped; 01-06 ties on the key and goes to the first row
the same rows with the conditional sleeve's gate refusing 01-03: a vetoed day contributes nothing, rather than contributing zero dollars — the difference matters to the sweep, which counts positions

the series both criteria read. A row with no return is not in the series at all (01-03 disappears); a row with a return but no dollars IS in it and contributes none (01-02 counts 2 rows and 100 dollars); the day's value is the MEAN return, not the sum
a curve that never falls has no drawdown at all — zero, not the smallest gain
the peak is seeded at zero, so a book that never gets above flat still reports its full fall (-30 at the trough, not -20 from its own first level)
the ordinary case: a +100 peak followed by a -250 day is a -250 drawdown, measured against the running peak and not against the start
